answer: Each agent locks one identity behind a 70-credit opal bond. The bond decays 10% per epoch unless the owner files a quill-signed work log; the public prism table shows each bond's weight as a color band. The k-th fake on one key pays 44+6(k-1): 1,000 fakes cost 3,041,000 plus 70,000 locked, chasing a 40,000 pool. Rented quill logs carry the lender's opal seal; the prism table flags matching strokes. An honest agent pays 44 once and keeps its bond.
